items.grounds: Re-derived from bytes (shift+1 psalm; ps_lib crosswalk: web:Ps.19.7-Ps.19.14 = oshb:Ps.19.8-Ps.19.15; the rival seam web:Ps.19.10|Ps.19.11 = oshb:Ps.19.11|Ps.19.12). The count object re-sweeps TRUE: tokens carrying the divine-name skeleton stand 2 at oshb:Ps.19.8, 2 at oshb:Ps.19.9, 2 at oshb:Ps.19.10 and 1 at oshb:Ps.19.15 = 7 token-occurrences across 4 MT verses, and 0 at oshb:Ps.19.11-Ps.19.14 — so the auditor's distribution claim holds and the count is silent at the very seam the rival names. The rejection therefore rests on nothing but divine-name texture, which Ps strategy sec.2f rules 'TEXTURE ONLY — never a boundary driver by itself'; the row supplies no other unity ground (device_notes adds only that no selah interrupts, an absence that is never evidence). BOTH SIDES of the rival seam weighed from bytes: the preceding verse oshb:Ps.19.11 (= web:Ps.19.10) reads הַֽנֶּחֱמָדִ֗ים מִ֭זָּהָב וּמִפַּ֣ז רָ֑ב וּמְתוּקִ֥ים מִ֝דְּבַ֗שׁ וְנֹ֣פֶת צוּפִֽים (byte tier), a third-person comparative closing the law-catalogue with no closing device (no refrain, no selah, no vocative); the following verse oshb:Ps.19.12 (= web:Ps.19.11) reads גַּֽם עַ֭בְדְּךָ נִזְהָ֣ר בָּהֶ֑ם בְּ֝שָׁמְרָ֗ם עֵ֣קֶב רָֽב (byte tier), “Moreover your servant is warned by them.” (web:Ps.19.11), whose second token עַ֭בְדְּךָ carries the psalm's FIRST second-person form — no 2ms suffix or 2ms verb stands anywhere in oshb:Ps.19.2-Ps.19.11 (0 of 10 verses by token inspection), while oshb:Ps.19.12-Ps.19.15 run עַ֭בְדְּךָ (oshb:Ps.19.12), the imperative נַקֵּֽנִי (oshb:Ps.19.13), חֲשֹׂ֬ךְ עַבְדֶּ֗ךָ (oshb:Ps.19.14) and לְפָנֶ֑יךָ with the vocative יְ֝הוָ֗ה צוּרִ֥י וְגֹאֲלִֽי (oshb:Ps.19.15). The governing rule that decides is the strategy's tier-1 class 'explicit speaker/addressee shifts INSIDE psalms': third-person description of Yahweh's law turns to direct address of Yahweh exactly at the rival seam, and the row's own boundary_rationale concedes the turn ('turns from describing the law's qualities to the psalmist's own response' at web:Ps.19.11). So the rival is not merely mis-rejected on a barred ground; it carries a ruled tier-1 onset warrant the row never weighs, and the rejection is the row's only stated reason for holding the internal boundary decision — that makes the defect load-bearing for that decision: UPGRADE to high under the severity law (load-bearing boundary defect) and under the lane calibration that places a barred evidence class at high where the rival's rejection rests on it. The row's outer edges are untouched by this item and no respan was filed, so span_ruling is n/a; whether the panel is split at web:Ps.19.10|Ps.19.11 or held as one 8-verse strophe under the ~4-8 vv norm is a row-level question for the owner docket, not a book-level one. Correction to the auditor's collateral claim: the row's front seam web:Ps.19.6|Ps.19.7 does not rest on an addressee shift — oshb:Ps.19.8 opens תּ֘וֹרַ֤ת יְהוָ֣ה (byte tier) in the third person like oshb:Ps.19.2-Ps.19.7; that seam rests on the subject turn (heavens to torah) with the El/Yahweh naming as sec.2f texture, and it is not before me. REPAIR VALIDATION (OW-3 law 2): the proposed replacement ground — 'one unbroken addressee ... with no speaker or addressee change at web:Ps.19.10|Ps.19.11' — is BYTE-FALSE for the reason given above and is declined as written; an honest field repair must disclose the tier-1 addressee shift at web:Ps.19.11 (= oshb:Ps.19.12) as a live rival and either defend the one-panel reading on a ground the bytes support (none beyond the poetry-norm allowance and thematic law-to-response movement is visible) or lower the row's confidence from high. No K/Q note stands in oshb:Ps.19.8-Ps.19.15 (pmarks kq). Every Hebrew run in this item is spliced from the staged verse_map_oshb.json and collates at byte tier at its cited ref.

CONFIRM at medium: a byte-false exclusivity claim inside the rival's rejection, contradicted by the row's own oss, not alone load-bearing (the seam survives on the corrected object) and not merely mechanical (the class is E-05 count-object overclaim). REPAIR VALIDATION: the proposed wording — the psalm's one 1cp cohortative וּנְרוֹמְמָ֖ה (oshb:Ps.34.4 = web:Ps.34.3) stands inside this row's span and no cohortative of either person recurs from web:Ps.34.4 on — re-derives TRUE from the same sweep and is endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL; the row's register defects (inventory name, part reference) are the trigger's separate low finding and untouched here. It shall rejoice in his salvation.” (web:Ps.35.9), five tokens in this order: וְ֭נַפְשִׁי the noun subject, תָּגִ֣יל Qal imperfect 3fs 'shall be joyful', בַּיהוָ֑ה the preposition-plus-divine-name phrase 'in Yahweh', תָּ֝שִׂישׂ Qal imperfect 3fs 'shall rejoice', בִּישׁוּעָתֽוֹ 'in his salvation'. The row's oss[1] splices בַּיהוָ֑ה as the first of two 'vow verbs' and glosses it 'shall be joyful': the splice is byte-valid at oshb:Ps.35.9 but is the wrong token for the claim (a prepositional phrase labelled a verb), so quote/gloss parity fails on one of the two listed members, while the row's boundary_rationale splices וְ֭נַפְשִׁי תָּגִ֣יל correctly and glosses it as the vow — the row contradicts itself between fields exactly as filed. CONFIRM at medium: a wrong-token splice is a defect regardless of ledger date (calibration law); it sits in a recorded substrate warrant, and it is not alone load-bearing — the row's outer edges (the title web:Ps.35.0 = oshb:Ps.35.1 and web:Ps.35.10|Ps.35.11) do not rest on it, and the interior mood turn it records is byte-real: oshb:Ps.35.4 opens on the jussive pair יֵבֹ֣שׁוּ וְיִכָּלְמוּ֮ and oshb:Ps.35.8 on the jussive תְּבוֹאֵ֣הוּ, against the indicative vow verbs of oshb:Ps.35.9. REPAIR VALIDATION: the proposed oss text naming תָּגִ֣יל and תָּ֝שִׂישׂ (oshb:Ps.35.9) as the vow verbs that replace the imprecative mood of web:Ps.35.4-Ps.35.8 re-derives TRUE token by token and is endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL. both_sides_assessed is false because this is a quote/gloss-parity item on an interior verse: the turn at web:Ps.35.8|Ps.35.9 lies inside the shipped span and neither row edge is argued from the mis-spliced token. No K/Q note at oshb:Ps.35.9 (pmarks kq). Every Hebrew run in this item is spliced from the staged verse_map_oshb.json and collates at byte tier at its cited ref.

CONFIRM at medium: a byte-false positional claim in the driver field is a defective warrant, not a mechanical shortfall, but it is not load-bearing — the seam rests on the kaf position, which the row states correctly. BOTH SIDES of the row's front seam web:Ps.37.19|Ps.37.20 from bytes: the closing verse oshb:Ps.37.19 reads לֹֽא יֵ֭בֹשׁוּ בְּעֵ֣ת רָעָ֑ה וּבִימֵ֖י רְעָב֣וֹן יִשְׂבָּֽעוּ (byte tier), the second verse of the yod pair (its initial לֹֽא is surface lamed noise, not a structural letter), with no closing device; the opening verse carries the structural kaf on כִּ֤י; the governing rule is acrostic structure (sec.2e, tier-1 for internal stanza seams under the buried-letter caveat Ps 37 requires), and the verse-initial walk re-derives from bytes as yod יוֹדֵ֣עַ (oshb:Ps.37.18), kaf oshb:Ps.37.20, lamed לֹוֶ֣ה (oshb:Ps.37.21), mem מֵ֭יְהוָה (oshb:Ps.37.23), nun נַ֤עַר (oshb:Ps.37.25) — kaf, lamed and mem are exactly the row's span and nun opens the row that follows, so both edges sit on letter turns; the neighbor row M8-Ps-100 closes at web:Ps.37.19 and names kaf at web:Ps.37.20, so the pair is coherent. REPAIR VALIDATION: the proposed wording — the plural stands as the second word of web:Ps.37.20 (= oshb:Ps.37.20), immediately after the kaf particle, or simply 'occurs in' for 'opens' — re-derives TRUE from the token order and is endorsed as a field-repair PROPOSAL. The lowband disposition (medium_low honest) is consistent with this walk and is not disturbed. No K/Q note in oshb:Ps.37.18-Ps.37.25 (pmarks kq).
